overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique Shorts reveals that speculative second-person survival hooks centered on extreme astronomical phenomena ('What If You Fell Into...') consistently drive FACTVERSE's highest reach (800-1,000+ views) and strongest like-per-view ratios (3.5%-3.7%). Videos around 19-21 seconds significantly outperform 12-16 second clips. Conversely, generic psychology trivia ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and repeated uploads ('Why Space Is Completely Silent') show severe audience fatigue, languishing under 60 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Space Hazard ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate top performance metrics.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme cosmic anomalies through visceral, second-person exploratory simulations where the viewer experiences the planetary environment directly.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' netted 981 views with 21 likes as the top recent performer, and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' garnered 1,028 views and 36 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Pair a mind-bending factual contradiction with tight 19-21 second pacing to ensure complete viewer retention and algorithm loop re-watches.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5 to 53 views with 0 likes, and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' produced only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire passive cognitive factoids unless framed within an intense high-stakes micro-story or dark psychological mystery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Duplicate Video Reposting Without Conceptual Iteration
weak_patterns.evidence: Posting identical topics such as 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' across three separate IDs yielded diminishing returns (down to 34 views).
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness rules; explore novel astronomical entities rather than recycling existing script premises.
